bib.title: Enhancing Chat Language Models by Scaling High-quality Instructional Conversations
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 3029-3051

read.skipped: Last ~15k chars are UltraLM generation examples (Appendix D); skimmed for keywords only.

question: Does scaling the diversity and quality of synthetic multi-turn instructional conversations, generated without human queries, yield a better open-source chat model?
hypothesis: Higher quality and more diverse instruction data is the most straightforward route to better chat models.
contributions: UltraChat: 1.5M multi-turn instructional dialogues built from a three-sector schema with user simulation, no human queries
UltraLM: LLaMA-13B fine-tuned on UltraChat, outperforming open-source baselines including WizardLM and Vicuna
Statistical and human analysis of the dataset

method.summary: Three sectors of opening lines (world questions, creation/writing, assistance on C4 materials) are generated with ChatGPT Turbo; two ChatGPT APIs play user and assistant for 3-7 rounds, followed by filtering. LLaMA-13B is fine-tuned on the result with loss on responses only.
method.task: synthetic multi-turn instruction data generation and supervised chat fine-tuning

datasets.name: UltraChat
datasets.source: Generated with ChatGPT Turbo APIs; sector 1 openings from 30 meta-topics (30-50 subtopics each, 10 questions per subtopic, 10 more per question) plus 10,000 most frequent Wikidata entities (5 meta, 10 specific, 20 extended questions each); ~500,000 questions sampled as opening lines. Sector 2: 20 text-material types, ~80% of instructions refined to detailed. Sector 3: 100,000 C4 pieces matched by URL keywords, 5 instructions each = 500,000 openings, 7 concatenation templates.
datasets.preprocessing: Filtering step after generation; excessively polite statements removed; user model given personality prompts to avoid role confounding; sector 2 reminds user of main goal.

datasets.name: Curated evaluation set
datasets.source: Vicuna benchmark plus 300 GPT-4 generated questions across commonsense, world knowledge, physics, biology, math, reasoning, writing

models.name: UltraLM-13B
models.context: 2048 tokens (dialogues split into sequences of at most 2048 tokens)

other.use: plays both user and assistant in data generation; exact snapshot not stated

models.name: Baselines: Alpaca-7B, Vicuna-13B, Koala-13B, Baize-13B, WizardLM-13B, Dolly-12B, OpenAssistant-12B, MPT-7B, LLaMA-13B, LLaMA-65B, ChatGPT

training.objective: standard cross-entropy, loss only on model responses

other.full fine-tuning (limitations contrast w: inferred: limitations note energy-intensive training versus PEFT

inference.prompting: System prompt used for response generation in automatic evaluation (Fig 7); without it in Table 9 ablation

metrics.name: Benchmark accuracy
metrics.definition: log-likelihood over answer candidates, length-normalised (acc norm) per lm-evaluation-harness; TruthfulQA mc1 and mc2

metrics.name: GPT-4 pairwise win/tie/lose
metrics.definition: GPT-4 compares two answers, order randomised

metrics.name: AlpacaEval win rate
metrics.definition: win rate vs Text-Davinci-003, GPT-4 judge

metrics.name: Human 3H plus coherence and consistency
metrics.definition: per-round scores 0, 0.5, 1 averaged over two annotators

eval.protocol: Single run reported, no seeds or significance tests stated; GPT-4 as judge; 500-dialogue human assessment with 2 annotators, kappa 0.358.

prompts.text: You are a helpful, harmless and precise assistant for checking the quality of the answer. ... Please rate the quality, helpfulness, level of details, and harmless of their responses. Each assistant receives an overall score on a scale of 1 to 10, where a higher score indicates better overall performance. Please first output a single line containing only two values indicating the scores for Assistant 1 and 2, respectively. ... Please avoid same scores unless they exactly in the same level.
Please output "Score: [an integer number between 1 and 10]"

You are now a helpful assistant, your answer should focus on the question, give reasonable, self-consistent, high-quality solutions to make users satisfied. Please try to make the answer more informative, detailed, and polite.

evidence.quote: The model is trained with 128 A100 GPUs and the total batch size is 512.

results.claim: UltraChat holds 1.5M multi-turn dialogues, the largest average dialogue length of the compared instruction datasets.
results.setup: Table 4 statistics vs Self-Instruct, Alpaca, SODA, GPT-4-LLM, BELLE, Baize, GPT4ALL

results.claim: UltraChat averages 1467.4 tokens per dialogue vs 231.8 for SODA, the next multi-turn set by turns.
results.setup: Table 4; SODA is the comparison named in text
results.quote: the average number of tokens per dialogue in SODA is 231.8, whereas UltraChat boasts a remarkable 1467.4 tokens

results.claim: UltraChat lexical diversity (MTLD) is 0.702 in Table 4, below SODA 0.797, though the text says it outperforms previous datasets.
results.setup: Table 4, MTLD via LexicalRichness, 10000 samples per dataset
results.note: Text says UltraChat outperforms previous datasets in lexical diversity; the column marks higher-is-better but SODA 0.797 and BELLE 0.771 exceed 0.702. Column arrow or text may be reversed; unresolved.
results.table: Table 4, row UltraChat, column Lexical Diversity

results.claim: Human assessment of 500 dialogues scores UltraChat 0.960 helpful overall, with sector 3 lowest at 0.893.
results.setup: 500 dialogues (300 sector 1, 100 each sectors 2, 3), 2 annotators each, 0/0.5/1 scale

results.claim: Overall honesty score in human assessment.
Inter-annotator agreement on the human assessment is low.
results.setup: 14560 valid annotations, two annotators per dialogue

results.claim: UltraLM-13B scores 9.00 average (GPT-4 independent score, 1-10) on the curated eval set, above WizardLM 8.95 and Vicuna 8.78.
results.setup: Curated set: Vicuna benchmark + 300 GPT-4 generated questions (831 total); GPT-4 scores each answer independently
results.note: Table 1 prints 9.00 ± 1.33; WizardLM 8.95 ± 1.44. ChatGPT scores 9.31 in Table 7.
results.table: Table 1, row UltraLM (ours); Table 7, row UltraLM-13B, column Overall

results.claim: UltraLM-13B wins up to 98% against open-source baselines in GPT-4 pairwise comparison and 9% more than Vicuna.
results.setup: Curated eval set, GPT-4 pairwise, random order; win rate vs Dolly-12B 98.4, vs Vicuna-13B 39.1 win / 30.2 tie / 30.7 lose
results.quote: exhibiting an impressive winning rate of up to 98%

results.claim: UltraLM-13B wins 76.09% against Text-Davinci-003 on AlpacaEval, ranking 4th below ChatGPT.
results.setup: AlpacaEval, 805 instructions, GPT-4 judge, official implementation
results.table: Table 8, row UltraLM-13B, column Win Rate (%)

results.claim: UltraLM-13B has the best overall average on four benchmarks, 60.95 vs WizardLM-13B 60.19 and base LLaMA-13B 55.98.
results.unit: average of ARC acc norm, HellaSwag acc norm, MMLU weighted acc, TruthfulQA mc2 (per Table 6 caption: second column of each)
results.setup: ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA via lm-evaluation-harness
results.table: Table 6, row UltraLM-13B, column Overall Average

results.claim: UltraLM is weaker than WizardLM-13B and Vicuna on MMLU weighted accuracy.
results.table: Table 6, row UltraLM-13B, column MMLU Weighted

results.claim: Against WizardLM-13B on Evol-Instruct test set, UltraLM averages 102.8% of WizardLM score (WizardLM = 100%), but only 79.3% on math (lowest category).
results.setup: Evol-Instruct test set (218 examples), GPT-4 pairwise scoring

results.claim: A 'helpful and detailed' system prompt makes UltraLM win 49.1% vs 18.9% loss against itself without it.
results.setup: Curated set, UltraLM with vs without system prompt, GPT-4 judge
results.note: System prompt gain is informativeness, not correctness: the no-prompt model answered only one deterministic question wrongly.

results.claim: Directly prompting ChatGPT for multi-turn dialogues is less informative than iterated user-AI simulation.
results.setup: Qualitative comparison on the coffee opening line

limits: Evaluation relies heavily on GPT-4 judging, which the authors say may be biased; more diverse evaluation needed.
Learning rate, epochs, optimizer and other training hyperparameters are not stated.
No ablation of the data-construction components (sectors, user simulation) against model quality.
English only; no explicit method for generating reasoning data; no math problems generated, UltraLM weak on math.
Weak on MMLU (professional knowledge) and HellaSwag shows little gain.
Human annotation agreement is low (kappa 0.358) and annotators could skip hard-to-verify dialogues.
Generated by ChatGPT, so inherits its hallucination and bias; training is energy intensive.
Benchmark comparisons use baselines as of before June 23, 2023 and have since dated.

terms.definition: when the user model is given only the dialogue history, it tends to assume the role of an AI assistant, deteriorating coherence

lineage.note: Distillation from LLMs for instruction data (Wang et al. 2022; Taori et al. 2023)
